newsitem.title: FINLAND: FOCUS-EMU to start on time with many countries - de Silguy.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-EMU to start on time with many countries - de Silguy.

text.p: European Union Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Friday he expected economic and monetary union to start on schedule and include many countries.
"It is clear that EMU will become reality starting January 1, 1999, and that a significant number of countries will join then," he told a news conference while on a visit to Finland.
"There is no turning back," he said. "That point has been crossed."

De Siguy said he could not predict "from any crystal ball" which or how many countries would form the currency union at the start, but that European growth had been strong this spring and many countries had shown "substantial budget discipline".
This reference included Italy, Spain and Portugal, he said in response to a question.

De Silguy said an assessment of which countries would qualify would be based on their meeting the five criteria in the Maastricht Treaty, looking at economic performance in 1997 "and on the tendency, which includes looking at budgets for 1998".
There would be "no fudging of the figures, no cooking of the books", he said.
De Silguy declined to comment on any individual country's chance of qualifying for monetary union, but said Finland was in a "very good position" to be in the first wave.

He also declined any comment on remarks made by Bank of France Council Member Paul Marchelli earlier on Friday about a desirable level for the planned euro. But he said the euro should be "a credible alternative to the dollar".
The dollar's position in international trade is much bigger than the weight of the U.S. trade would justify. "That system in not stable," he said.
Asked to comment on risks of instability in currency markets in the run-up to the launch of EMU in 1999, he said this was a problem but that each country's fiscal policy was key to stability.

"The most important is that tight budget policy is maintained," he said. The final decisions on which countries will join EMU at the start would be made within a short time span next spring to counter speculation, he added
